name: Karl Lopez

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I’m with the Work Futures Panel, an independent research group with no ties to AI companies, employers, unions, political parties or government. We sell nothing and campaign for no side. This interview is confidential. What does an ordinary day at the contact centre look like for you?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I am 43, have a two-year college diploma, and lead the late complaints desk. I can usually untangle a disputed bill while the caller is still there, and I coach newer agents through the harder cases. I never use AI tools; I want the account record in front of me. The wage is low for this job despite the responsibility.

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: What follows you home from that desk?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: My partner Elias and I have two children in school and a mortgage, with only three weeks of expenses saved. He fixes kitchen equipment on short contracts. I remember the caller whose electricity payment went to the wrong account; a solved ticket was not a solved bill. There are few comparable centre jobs nearby.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau. Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d tell the desk that AI Plateau leaves most complaints with us. I would still ask our staff group to challenge a speed target that counts a reopened bill as finished.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I think my skill keeps the late desk useful, but our three-week reserve makes every broken appliance a problem. Elias’s contract work can go quiet without warning.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: In 2026 I’d keep leading complaint calls and record reopened electricity bills by hand. In the first year of minor change, I’d join the staff group in asking management to stop treating reopenings as resolved calls, and put the cost of one takeaway a week into our mortgage buffer.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious about the money, even with no great AI change. Three weeks of savings is one repair away from nothing.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Which bill would you take to the group?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would bring the group the account number with the customer’s name removed. The payment was found only when I read the second page of the record.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you cut at home?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell Elias (my partner) that the takeaway money is the first easy cut. We will still pay for the children’s school lunches.

say: I’d say **human complaints** still need my careful account checks in AI Plateau.
I’d ask colleagues to challenge **false closure targets** together.
think: I think my **desk skill** remains useful.
I worry our **three-week reserve** cannot absorb a repair or Elias’s lost contract.
do: Keep **leading complaint calls** and log reopened electricity bills in 2026.
Join the **staff group demand** against false closures; skip one weekly takeaway and transfer its cost into the mortgage buffer.
S0.quote: Three weeks of savings is one repair away from nothing.
fieldNote: His **skill** protects work more than his savings protect income.
He challenges **closure targets** with a customer record.
He protects **school lunches** while trimming takeaways.

steps.text: Keep leading complaint calls and log reopened electricity bills

Save the cost of one takeaway each week for mortgage bills
Skip one weekly takeaway while protecting children's school lunches

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption. Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d tell colleagues Steady Disruption will strip out simple chats before anyone announces a lost job. I would join their request for written paid hours by shift and a human route for wrong bills.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I think my escalations might last longer than routine calls, but fewer paid late shifts could still hurt us. I cannot put the mortgage on Elias’s uneven contracts.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: In 2026 I’d help the staff group deliver a written demand for shift hours and customer appeals. In the first year routine chats move, I’d apply for a posted paid dispute role only if its written weekly wage and hours cover our mortgage; I would keep this job until a signed offer arrives.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious and cross with the way a quiet cut can look harmless. Losing two late shifts would be a wage cut without a redundancy letter.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How would you show a cut?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would put the last six late rotas beside the new one. A monthly total hides which families lost evening pay.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you take a course?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask for the vacancy itself before studying anything new. An unpaid course cannot make our next mortgage payment.

say: I’d warn that **routine chats** may leave before jobs formally vanish.
I’d join a **written group demand** for paid hours and customer appeals.
think: I think my **escalation skill** may last longer than simple chats.
I fear lost **late shifts** would strain our mortgage.
do: Help demand **written shift hours** and customer appeals together in 2026.
Apply for **posted dispute work** only with written mortgage-covering weekly wage and hours; stay until a signed offer.
feel: **Anxious** and angry about quiet pay cuts.
S1.quote: Losing two late shifts would be a wage cut without a redundancy letter.
fieldNote: He distinguishes **paid shifts** from a formal job loss.
A real **posted vacancy** matters more than an unpaid course.
The **mortgage** depends on his wage, not Elias’s uncertain contracts.

steps.text: Help staff group demand written paid hours by shift and customer appeals
Apply for posted dispute work with mortgage-covering written pay and hours; stay until signed offer

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028. Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d say AGI by 2028 can do the whole disputed account, not only type a reply. I would ask colleagues to demand written notice, paid hours and a customer appeal route before the late desk is cut.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I think my best judgment may not protect this job in 2028. Robots around 2031 come too late to matter to a headset, and three weeks saved will not carry a search.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: In 2026 I’d join the group demand for written notice and appeals and stop the planned sofa purchase. In the first year after 2028, I’d seek a posted paid records role only if its written wage and hours cover our mortgage, keeping my current wage until a signed offer; I’d take a required records course only if funded on paid time for that vacancy.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Alarmed, because the calendar is shorter than our debt. I cannot turn a three-week buffer into a year of searching by being careful.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What happens to the sofa?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would show Elias (my partner) the sofa can wait; the old one still holds together. We would keep the money for mortgage and school costs.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What terms would make training possible?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would need the posted opening, the course fee covered, and paid hours to attend. A certificate without an opening would only leave us with less cash.

say: I’d say **2028 AGI** threatens the whole disputed account.
I’d demand **notice and appeals** with colleagues before shifts disappear.
think: I think my **judgment** may not protect the late desk.
I know **three weeks saved** cannot fund a long search.
do: Join a **group notice demand** and defer the usable sofa in 2026.
Seek **posted records work** after 2028 only at written mortgage-covering wage and hours; keep current work until signed offer.
Take **required records training** only if funded on paid time for that posted vacancy.
S2.quote: I cannot turn a three-week buffer into a year of searching by being careful.
fieldNote: The **2028 thinking-work deadline** matters more than 2031 robots.
His **sofa deferral** keeps cash for bills.
Training depends on a **posted paid vacancy**, funding and paid time.

steps.text: Join colleagues demanding written notice, paid hours and customer appeals

Seek posted records work after 2028 with mortgage-covering written pay and hours; stay until signed offer
Take required records course only if funded on paid time for posted paid records vacancy

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031. Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d say AGI by 2031 gives us time to win proper paid training for real vacancies. I would ask our staff group to demand the posted role, course hours and wage in one document.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I think I could move into records review if it is still paid work, though full AGI may take that too. Five years lets us save a little, but our mortgage cannot wait through unpaid study.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: From 2026 I’d join the group demand for funded records-review training on paid time and take that course only if a posted paid vacancy requires it. In the first year after 2031, I’d apply for that vacancy only with written mortgage-covering weekly wage and hours, keeping my late desk until I have a signed offer.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious, with a bit more room to insist on terms. Five years lets me ask for a wage before I sit in a classroom.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What must the course teach?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would want to correct an actual payment record during class, with a trainer checking my work. I have seen a tidy case note conceal a missing payment.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Why a group document?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask the group to put the paid study hours in writing. A promise made between shifts disappears when the rota changes.

say: I’d demand **paid training** for posted roles in one group document.
I’d ask for a **written wage** before enrolling.
think: I think **records review** might offer a paid route.
I know **full AGI** could threaten that route too.
do: Join a **group training demand** and take required funded records training on paid time for a posted paid vacancy.
Apply for **posted records work** after 2031 only with written mortgage-covering weekly wage and hours; keep current job until signed offer.
feel: **Anxious**, but able to insist on terms.
S3.quote: Five years lets me ask for a wage before I sit in a classroom.
fieldNote: He wants **real payment errors** in the course.
The **posted vacancy** and paid study hours are conditions, not hopes.
He would retain his **current wage** until a signed offer.

steps.text: Join group demand for funded paid-time records training tied to posted vacancy

Apply for posted records role after 2031 with written mortgage-covering pay/hours; stay until signed offer

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036. Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d say AGI by 2036 gives us a decade to make paid appeals and written hours normal practice. I would keep asking the staff group to bring those terms to management each year.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I think I can still lead the late desk and put money aside for years, but cheap thinking AI could take complaints in 2036. Robots around 2039 do not delay that risk for a call worker.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: In 2026 I’d keep leading calls, save a fixed amount from each wage and join the group’s annual request for written late-shift hours and appeals. In the first year after 2036, I’d apply for posted paid dispute work only if my hours fall and its written weekly wage and hours cover the mortgage, staying at my desk until a signed offer.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Uneasy about the far end, anxious enough about this month’s bills. Ten years is time to build a reserve, not permission to ignore the next rota.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you save first?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would save a fixed amount before paying for anything optional. The children still need their bus fares and school meals.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would the group count?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask for late hours by person, with names removed. A centre total could rise while half the experienced agents lose shifts.

say: I’d seek **written late hours** through the staff group each year.
think: I think I can **lead and save** for years.
I know **2036 thinking AI** may still take complaints.
do: Keep **leading calls**, save from each wage and join annual group demands for late hours and appeals.
Apply for **posted dispute work** after 2036 if hours fall, with written mortgage-covering pay and hours; stay until signed offer.
feel: **Uneasy** about 2036 and anxious about current bills.
S4.quote: Ten years is time to build a reserve, not permission to ignore the next rota.
fieldNote: His **thin cushion** keeps today’s bills salient under the 2036 scenario.
He wants **late hours by person**, not a centre total.
His job move needs **written mortgage-covering terms**.

steps.text: Keep leading late complaint calls while the centre staffs them

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 frightens me most because it can take the whole complaints desk before we can save another month. Written notice, a group agreement on paid hours and appeals, and a real paid vacancy with a wage and hours that cover the mortgage would help. If that vacancy requires a course, the employer must fund it on paid time.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn't ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: You did not ask who calls the customer back when an automatic answer closes a wrong bill. A closed ticket cannot explain a missed electricity payment.

headlineQuote: A closed ticket cannot explain a missed electricity payment.
portrait: At **43**, Karl leads difficult complaints after a two-year college diploma but earns low pay.
He and Elias support **two schoolchildren** and a mortgage with only three weeks saved.
He avoids **AI tools** and relies on account records and coaching.
He seeks **shared paid-hour terms** as thinking work moves to software.
biggestWorry: **AGI by 2028** could erase his complaints desk before the household builds another month of savings.
whatWouldHelp: **Written notice**, shared paid-hour and appeal terms, and mortgage-covering posted work would help.
